subject: Private deploy commercial structure: SKU splits, tiered rebates, and cross-account anchoring

Subject: Inquiry: Private deploy pricing and packaging for multi-account rollout

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked the latency and observability story. We're starting to scope a private/VPC rollout spanning three business units (CareOps, Analytics, Clinical Apps) and procurement asked for a clear commercial model so they can budget in Q3. High-level asks: 

- Can you outline packaging options (operator/site license vs node-based) for an on-prem pilot that converts to multi-account VPC?
- How do you amortize the platform fee across accounts and time (pilot -> prod)?
- Any discount/rebate structures for cross-account anchored volume (we expect combined token volumes of ~1.2B/month within 12 months if adoption goes well)

I've attached a short rollout overview (ClearPath_Rollout_Overview.pdf). Procurement would like a ballpark by end of next week. Also flagging Helen (CFO) on timing/approval.

Budget is constrained — they'd prefer a staged commercial path with predictable TCO. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Sam

ClearPath Health

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Inquiry: Private deploy pricing and packaging for multi-account rollout

Sam —

Appreciate the context and the overview doc. Quick high-level framing so procurement has something to react to before we do a full TCO exercise: 

Option A — Operator / Site license (pilot ->-prod convert):
- Fixed platform fee (covers control plane, observability, support).
- Operator licenses per site for on-prem nodes if they need dedicated operator tooling.
- Best when you want predictable fixed costs and limited burst.
- Typical amortization: platform fee split across initial pilot (3–6 months) then rolled into annual committed invoice.

Option B — Node / capacity + usage floor (commit + overage):
- Commit to node capacity (GPU-equivalent) and pay token-based overage.
- Lower upfront platform fee; more aligned to consumption.
- Works if volumes ramp quickly and you want to avoid large platform prepay.

Rebates / cross-account anchoring: we can offer timebound volume rebates structured as: 1) 10–15% rebate on platform fee when combined accounts hit X tokens and a 12-month committed minimum, or 2) a graduated discount that increases as you cross 3 volume tiers. We can also offer limited implementation credits if you commit to an 18-month term and provide a single SOW covering all accounts.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Share a short usage profile (expected Q1/Q2 monthly tokens, peak seq length, expected concurrency) so we can run the TCO model.
2) I’ll loop in Marissa from Commercial to propose an initial pricing grid and term options.
3) We prepare an SOW draft and example amortization schedule.

Attaching a quick TCO template we use to illustrate amortization and platform fee pooling — I can pre-fill with rough assumptions if you want.

Would you be available Wed 14th 09:00 PT for 30 min?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
(attachment: TCO_model.xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy commercial structure: SKU splits, tiered rebates, and cross-account anchoring

Sean / Sam —

Following Sean's framing, attached is a concise commercial grid with concrete examples. Key proposal (initial):

- Platform fee: $120k/year, amortizable across accounts. Pilot credit: we discount first 3 months of platform fee by 50% if they sign a 12-month conversion commitment.
- Operator license: $18k/site/year for up to 4 operator seats.
- Node equivalent: $9k per vGPU-month (committed) with token overages at $0.000012/token.
- Cross-account rebate: 15% rebate on platform fee (credited on renewal) if combined monthly tokens >= 900M for three consecutive months and a minimum 12-month committed term across accounts.

Conditional implementation credit: $30k implementation credit if ClearPath signs a consolidated SOW covering the three business units and pays first invoice within 45 days. Credit applied to final invoice over first 6 months.

Open items we need from ClearPath to finalize:
- Confirmation of pilot duration (3 vs 6 months)
- Expected ramp (month-by-month) for tokens and concurrency
- Any regulatory or air-gap requirements that change operating footprint

I've attached the commercial-grid.csv and included a simple amortization example in the sheet. If that high-level bundle looks acceptable we can produce a pricing schedule for procurement and a clean SOW (ClearPath_SOW_draft_v3.pdf).

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Commercial Manager — Redwood Inference
(attachment: commercial-grid.csv)
